```{r}
#| label: registry
#| include: false
# Standard: key on athlete id, never name (recruiting ids collide, decision 0013).
# The cfb_athlete_id here are the shared CFBD athlete namespace; each was resolved
# from the cleaned player_stats by name and QA-verified by its season/team pattern
# below; this post does not generalize the name lookup.
subjects <- tibble::tribble(
  ~who                 , ~cfb_athlete_id , ~gsis_id    ,
  "Arch Manning"       , "4870906"       , NA_character_,
  "Nicco Marchiol"     , "4685459"       , NA_character_,
  "Jordan Travis"      , "4360799"       , "00-0039797",
  "Cam Ward"           , "4688380"       , "00-0040676",
  "Trinidad Chambliss" , "4911529"       , NA_character_,
  "Joe Burrow"         , "3915511"       , "00-0036442",
  "Malachi Nelson"     , "4870928"       , NA_character_
)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
*Data as of the `data-latest` release, retrieved 2026-10-17. Careers of recent
classes (Manning, Marchiol, Chambliss, Nelson, Ward's Titans tenure) are
right-censored; later seasons may not yet be present.*

## 1. Introduction

Widely held expectations about individual player careers are, in principle,
testable claims against the data this project curates. This post evaluates
narrative expectations for seven quarterbacks whose careers are commonly
described with confidence: a redshirt-freshman-slash-double-medical-redshirt
at two schools, a player described as having redshirted and then transferred
on his way to the #1 overall selection, a five-year quarterback whose college
career ended with injury, three multi-transfer quarterbacks of the portal
era, and the most heavily publicized recruit of recent memory.

The premise of the exercise is that each expectation can be translated into a
statement about what the database should contain, and then evaluated against
what it does contain. A claim about the data should either survive contact
with the tables or fail in an explicit and diagnosable way. Accordingly, the
results below are reported as a ledger, including cases where the honest
conclusion is that the data cannot observe the phenomenon in question, which
is itself a result, and one case that surfaced a defect in the data.

## 2. Data

```{r}
#| label: build-spine
#| include: false
con <- dbConnect(duckdb(), "data/cfbstats.duckdb", read_only = TRUE)
ids_sql <- paste(sprintf("'%s'", subjects$cfb_athlete_id), collapse = ",")

# Roster backbone + eligibility flags (derived table, decision 0021).
flags <- dbGetQuery(con, sprintf(
  "SELECT playerId, season, team, position, class_year, has_stats,
          redshirt_season, redshirt_career, fifth_year_career
   FROM roster_flags WHERE playerId IN (%s) ORDER BY playerId, season", ids_sql))
flags <- flags |>
  mutate(who = subjects$who[match(playerId, subjects$cfb_athlete_id)])

career <- dbGetQuery(con, sprintf(
  "SELECT * FROM career_summary WHERE playerId IN (%s)", ids_sql)) |>
  mutate(who = subjects$who[match(playerId, subjects$cfb_athlete_id)])

college_picks <- dbGetQuery(con, sprintf(
  "SELECT CAST(collegeAthleteId AS VARCHAR) AS pid, year, round, pick, overall,
          name, nflTeam FROM picks WHERE CAST(collegeAthleteId AS VARCHAR) IN (%s)",
  ids_sql))
dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

# Usage: passing attempts per season from the long stats table.
stats <- open_dataset("data/player_stats.parquet") |>
  filter(playerId %in% subjects$cfb_athlete_id) |>
  select(playerId, season, team, category, statType, stat) |>
  collect()
attempts <- stats |>
  filter(category == "passing", statType == "ATT") |>
  transmute(playerId, season, attempts = as.numeric(stat))

spine <- flags |>
  left_join(attempts, by = c("playerId", "season")) |>
  # CFBD id reuse is excluded from career populations (decision 0022); assert
  # none of these subjects were caught by that exclusion.
  left_join(career |> select(who, seasons, teams, transfers, gap_seasons), by = "who")

stopifnot(
  nrow(spine) > 0,
  all(subjects$who %in% spine$who),
  !anyNA(spine$has_stats),
  # A missing attempts value should occur only on a no-stat (redshirt-shaped)
  # season; assert that, so the figure's "RS" label is never a lie.
  all(is.na(spine$attempts) == !spine$has_stats)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: team-colors
#| include: false
teams <- open_dataset("data/teams.parquet") |>
  select(team, color) |>
  collect()
spine <- spine |>
  left_join(teams, by = c("team" = "team")) |>
  # FCS/D2 programs can sit outside teams.parquet; fall back to gray.
  mutate(color = if_else(is.na(color), "#9CA3AF", color),
         tooltip = paste0(who, " · ", team, " · ", season,
                          if_else(is.na(attempts), "", paste0(" · ", attempts, " pass att"))))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-timeline
#| fig-cap: "Season-by-season college timelines for the seven subjects, in team colors. The number is passing attempts that season; 'RS' marks a redshirt-SHAPED flag (a no-stat season followed by another observed season). The hole in Trinidad Chambliss's row is a missing 2024; the database has no Ferris State roster row for the season he won a Division II national championship."
rel_lum <- function(hex) {
  m <- grDevices::col2rgb(hex) / 255
  lin <- ifelse(m <= 0.03928, m / 12.92, ((m + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4)
  0.2126 * lin[1, ] + 0.7152 * lin[2, ] + 0.0722 * lin[3, ]
}
p <- ggplot(spine, aes(x = season, y = who)) +
  geom_tile_interactive(
    aes(fill = color, tooltip = tooltip, data_id = paste(who, season)),
    color = "white", height = 0.75
  ) +
  geom_text_interactive(
    aes(label = if_else(is.na(attempts), "RS", as.character(attempts)),
        data_id = paste(who, season)),
    color = if_else(rel_lum(spine$color) < 0.5, "white", "#111827"),
    size = 3.2, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2014:2026) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_cfbstats(base_size = 14) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "none")
girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 9.5, height_svg = 4)
```

The analysis spine joins, for each subject and season, the roster backbone
and its eligibility flags, per-season passing attempts from
the long statistics table, and the derived career summary. Figure 1 displays
the resulting timelines; Table 1 reports the per-career summaries the
pipeline derives from that backbone.

```{r}
#| label: career-table
career |>
  select(who, seasons, first_season, last_season, teams, transfers, gap_seasons) |>
  kable(caption = "Career summaries from the roster backbone.")
```

## 3. Results

### 3.1 Arch Manning, Texas: current player

*Expectation: playing for Texas, first in a reserve role, then becoming a
starter.*

```{r}
#| label: arch-table
spine |> filter(who == "Arch Manning") |>
  select(season, team, class_year, has_stats, attempts) |>
  kable(caption = "Arch Manning, season by season.")
```

The expectation is confirmed. The data contain four
Texas seasons, 2023 through 2026, all within the observed window. However,
the reserve period is not binary in these data: he recorded 5 pass attempts
in 2023 and 90 in 2024, before 404 in 2025. The `has_stats` flag is TRUE for
the reserve seasons, so his apprenticeship does not resemble a redshirt under
this definition; it resembles a reserve season with measurable passing
volume. Defining a "backup season" feature would therefore require an
attempts threshold rather than a stat-presence flag, a design choice this
analysis motivates.

### 3.2 Nicco Marchiol, West Virginia then Northwestern: two expected redshirts

*Expectation: redshirting as a freshman at West Virginia, later taking a
medical redshirt there, then transferring to Northwestern.*

```{r}
#| label: marchiol-table
spine |> filter(who == "Nicco Marchiol") |>
  select(season, team, has_stats, attempts, redshirt_season) |>
  kable(caption = "Nicco Marchiol, season by season.")
```

The data show no redshirt-shaped season at all: zero redshirt-shaped flags,
zero gap seasons, and five consecutive roster seasons each with a stat line.
The external record indicates the redshirts occurred, but the observable
quantities here are 13 pass attempts in 2022, then 53, 56, and 98. A medical
redshirt after appearing in four games with 56 attempts leaves a stat line,
and a stat line is the only evidence available to `has_stats` and the
redshirt flag. That flag is explicitly redshirt-*shaped* rather than
certified. This case demonstrates that
limitation: two known redshirts,
zero flags. The flag detects quiet seasons; it cannot detect quiet careers.

### 3.3 Jordan Travis, Louisville then Florida State: injury, draft selection, no subsequent NFL play

*Expectation: redshirting at Louisville, playing five years at Florida State
with the COVID season extending eligibility, suffering a late-season injury
in his final year, being drafted anyway, and never playing another NFL snap.*

```{r}
#| label: travis-table
spine |> filter(who == "Jordan Travis") |>
  select(season, team, has_stats, attempts) |>
  kable(caption = "Jordan Travis, season by season. Note two rows for 2021.")
```

The expectation is mostly confirmed, with one correction and one artifact.

The correction concerns Louisville: he did not redshirt there, he played,
recording 14 pass attempts in 2018. The commonly stated version of the
expectation ("redshirted at Louisville") is contradicted by the stat line.
The more precise account is a mid-career transfer following a season spent
mostly in a reserve role. The 2019 Florida State season shows 11 attempts,
consistent with his own injury year, followed by 131, 194, 353, and 324.

The artifact is more consequential. Two rows exist for 2021: Florida State
*and* Louisville. Jordan Travis did not play at Louisville in 2021. This
duplicate propagates into every
downstream join, and his derived counts inherit the duplication. It
indicates a missing uniqueness guarantee on `(playerId, season, team)`.

The NFL outcome is unambiguous. He was
selected in round 5, pick 171 overall, 2024, by New York, and appears on Jets
rosters in 2024 and 2025 with zero rows in the NFL player-stats table. The
absence of rows meets our expectations because while drafted he never
played. The absence is the finding: a roster presence is not a snap, and
injured reserve status also produces roster rows. Right-censoring does not
complicate the interpretation here; six seasons of comparable stat rows are
one identifier away for a contemporary quarterback, and Travis has none.

### 3.4 Cam Ward, Incarnate Word, Washington State, Miami, then the Titans: the multi-transfer

*Expectation: playing for three schools, then being selected first overall.*

```{r}
#| label: ward-table
spine |> filter(who == "Cam Ward") |>
  select(season, team, has_stats, attempts) |>
  kable(caption = "Cam Ward, season by season.")

college_picks |> filter(pid == "4688380") |>
  select(year, round, pick, overall, nflTeam) |>
  kable(caption = "Cam Ward's draft slot (CFBD picks).")
```

The transfer sequence is confirmed exactly: three schools, two transfers,
four roster seasons, and selection first overall in 2025. His FCS origin,
however, is where the data are weakest. There is no 2020 row at all, the
COVID-fallout FCS season that Incarnate Word played in spring 2021, and the
2021 season shows only 47 pass attempts for a player who produced one of the
most prolific FCS passing seasons on record. CFBD's per-player stat coverage
for lower divisions is partial. Two consequences follow. First,
Ward's college totals in these data undercount his production. Second, and
more important for the modeling objective, FCS and Division 2 origins
systematically produce thin or absent early seasons, so any "career shape"
feature will misclassify players such as Ward and Chambliss as late starters
rather than as under-covered.

The recruiting table does not contain Cam Ward at all. He was genuinely
unranked out of high school, and "unrated" is a real category rather than an
imputation target.

### 3.5 Trinidad Chambliss, Ferris State then Ole Miss: Division 2 to the SEC

```{r}
#| label: chambliss-table
spine |> filter(who == "Trinidad Chambliss") |>
  select(season, team, has_stats, attempts, redshirt_season) |>
  kable(caption = "Trinidad Chambliss, season by season.")
```

Our expectation is starting at Ferris State (Division 2) then transferring to
Ole Miss. The transfers are confirmed; the 2024 season is not. The 2023
season at Ferris State carries a redshirt-shaped flag, with no stats followed
by observed seasons. 2024 is missing entirely: no roster row, no stat line.
The derived career summary
records this as `gap_seasons = 1`, which is the incorrect conclusion; that
"gap" is the season in which he started and won a Division II national
championship. CFBD's roster coverage does not reach Division 2 for 2024.

This case demonstrates why `gap_seasons` requires a companion coverage
measure before becoming a feature: a gap flag computed over a
coverage-limited table measures coverage at least as much as it measures
careers. Chambliss is not an edge case; he is the starting quarterback of a
top-ranked SEC team at the time of writing.

### 3.6 Joe Burrow, Ohio State then LSU: redshirt, transfer, first overall selection

```{r}
#| label: burrow-table
spine |> filter(who == "Joe Burrow") |>
  select(season, team, has_stats, attempts, redshirt_season) |>
  kable(caption = "Joe Burrow, season by season.")

college_picks |> filter(pid == "3915511") |>
  select(year, round, pick, overall, nflTeam) |>
  kable(caption = "Joe Burrow's draft slot (CFBD picks).")
```

*Expectation: redshirting at Ohio State, then transferring to LSU and being
selected first overall.*

Here the data flag two seasons as redshirts, 2014 and 2015. Only 2014 was a
redshirt; Burrow was
an active backup who happened to record zero of any statistic the feed
carries (2016 shows 28 attempts, 2017 shows 11). A stat-presence flag cannot
distinguish "redshirted" from "dressed and never targeted." The case
therefore confirms the mechanism and exposes its false-positive rate: one
real redshirt, two flags. Any feature built on `redshirt_season` inherits a
known, quantifiable over-count, which is preferable to know before modeling.

His recruiting row is also absent. The class of 2015 falls within the
recruiting table's 2010-2026 span, so this is a coverage or name-resolution
miss rather than a range problem. The #1 pick in the data's own draft table
has no recruiting record; this warrants an issue.

### 3.7 Malachi Nelson, USC, Boise State, UTEP, then Syracuse: the other multi-transfer

```{r}
#| label: nelson-table
spine |> filter(who == "Malachi Nelson") |>
  select(season, team, has_stats, attempts) |>
  kable(caption = "Malachi Nelson, season by season.")
```

*Expectation: redshirting at USC, then transferring through the portal
repeatedly.*

The transfers are confirmed exactly: four teams and three transfers, the
largest transfer count in this sample. The redshirt is invisible because
2023 shows 3 pass attempts, which
a flag built on stat presence reads as a played season. Combined with
Marchiol (two real redshirts, zero flags) and Burrow (zero-volume backup,
two flags), the pattern is that usage, not presence, is the observable
quantity, and eligibility events are not. A redshirt proxy must therefore be
defined by attempts and games thresholds with an explicit uncertainty band,
or it will be incorrect in both directions.

## 4. Summary of findings

| Expectation | Data verdict |
|---|---|
| Arch Manning is at Texas now | Confirmed: 4 seasons, with a 5, 90, 404-attempt apprenticeship |
| Marchiol redshirted twice | **Invisible**: stat lines every season; redshirt-shaped flags detect quiet seasons, not quiet usage |
| Travis redshirted at Louisville | **Contradicted**: he recorded 14 attempts there in 2018 |
| Travis: 5 FSU years, injured, drafted, no NFL snaps | Confirmed: draft slot present, Jets rosters 2024-2025, zero NFL stat rows |
| Ward: 3 transfers to the #1 pick | Confirmed, but his FCS years are under-covered (no 2020, 47 attempts in 2021), and he is absent from recruiting entirely |
| Chambliss: Ferris State then Ole Miss | Confirmed with a hole: the 2024 D2 championship season is a missing row recorded as a "gap" |
| Burrow: redshirt then transfer to #1 pick | Confirmed and **over-flagged**: two redshirt-shaped seasons for one real redshirt |
| Nelson: USC redshirt then 3 transfers | Transfers confirmed (4 teams); the redshirt is invisible behind 3 attempts |

## 5. Discussion

One finding from this analysis remains open in the pipeline:

1. **Redshirt flags require a usage-based definition** (attempts and games
   thresholds) rather than stat presence. Marchiol, Nelson, and Burrow
   collectively exhibit every failure mode. *Still open.*

The database satisfied most of the stated expectations, which is the least
informative of the results. The informative results are the three modes in
which it is *structurally* blind: quiet usage, lower-division coverage, and
a corrupted eligibility column. These are the failure shapes most likely to
bias the model this project exists to build, and they are invisible without
exactly this kind of targeted validation.
